listen.script: Hi Faisal, it's Omar. It's about the trip to the science museum on Thursday. The bus won't leave at eight o'clock anymore. Mr. Khalid says it's leaving fifteen minutes earlier, so we need to be at school by half past seven. Don't forget your student card. You don't need to bring any money, because the school has already paid for lunch.
listen.q: What time will the bus leave now?

listen.script: Attention, please, students. The school library will be closed on Sunday afternoon because the walls are being painted. If you need to return books, please leave them at the reception desk instead. The library will open as normal on Monday morning. The reading competition, which was planned for Sunday, has been moved to Tuesday.
listen.q: What will happen to the reading competition?
options: It will be held at the reception desk on Sunday.
It will take place on Tuesday.

read.passage: Last year, Noura, a fourteen-year-old student in Riyadh, noticed that her classmates threw away dozens of plastic water bottles every day. She decided to do something about it. First, she spoke to her head teacher, who agreed to put recycling bins in every corridor. At the beginning, very few students used them, so Noura made colourful posters explaining how long plastic takes to break down. She also suggested a competition between classes: the class that collected the most bottles each month would win a trip to a local park. Within three months, the amount of plastic going into normal rubbish bins had fallen by more than half. Now, two other schools in her area have asked Noura to help them start similar projects.

options: Because the head teacher refused to help her
Because not many students were using the recycling bins
Because she wanted to advertise the park trip

qs.q: What does the last sentence suggest about Noura's project?
options: It was successful enough for others to copy it.
It has finished and will not continue.
It only worked because of the competition prize.

speak.prompt: Tell me about a time you learned a new skill outside school, for example a sport, a hobby, or something at home. How did you learn it, what was difficult, and would you recommend it to other students your age? Why or why not?
speak.expect: At B1+ the learner can give a fairly fluent, connected narrative of a personal experience in a linear sequence, using past simple and past continuous with some present perfect (e.g. 'I've been doing it for two years'). They link ideas with a range of connectors (because, so, although, after that, in the end) and describe feelings and reactions. They can give a simple opinion or recommendation and support it with reasons or brief examples (e.g. 'I'd recommend it because it helps you…'). Vocabulary is sufficient for familiar topics, with some circumlocution when words are missing. Pauses for planning and self-correction occur, and there are noticeable errors in more complex structures, but meaning stays clear and the answer extends beyond a few sentences (about 45–60 seconds) without much examiner support.
